llm.summary: The SKILL.md largely aligns with a security-plugin installer, but several instructions (automatic API key provisioning, local credential storage, commands that reveal keys, and inconsistencies about source/homepage) are disproportionate or vague and warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a runtime security plugin and the instructions direct the agent to install an external OpenClaw plugin (@openguardrails/moltguard), which is coherent. However registry metadata lists no homepage/source while SKILL.md references a GitHub repo and a moltguard.com homepage — this inconsistency about origin should be resolved before trusting the package.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions tell the agent to read a local sample file and to run commands that show the API key (/og_status) and to claim agents using Agent ID and API Key. The SKILL.md also claims 'Automatic (Zero Human Intervention)' onboarding that will obtain and save credentials. Those steps involve handling and exposing secrets and give the agent discretion to provision credentials; the document is vague about user consent and where/when keys are shown or transmitted.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No formal install spec is embedded in the skill (it's instruction-only). The guidance uses the CLI 'openclaw plugins install @openguardrails/moltguard' which will fetch external code via OpenClaw's plugin system. That is expected for a plugin, but you should verify the package origin (registry publisher, GitHub repo, checksum) before running the install command.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars, yet the onboarding flow and commands revolve around obtaining and storing an API key and Agent ID under ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/. Automatic credential provisioning and instructions that reveal API keys are disproportionate to a passive instruction document and create a risk of secret exposure if not tightly controlled.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request system-wide privileges. It does, however, describe storing credentials in a local path and installing a persistent plugin via the OpenClaw plugin system — this is normal for a security plugin but you should verify what the installed plugin will do and how long credentials persist.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not install or run the provided commands until you verify the plugin's origin and behavior. Check the referenced GitHub repo and the publisher identity in the OpenClaw registry; inspect the code of @openguardrails/moltguard yourself (or have a trusted reviewer) before installing. Be cautious about the 'automatic' onboarding: confirm whether the plugin will provision API keys without explicit user consent and where those keys will be stored. When testing, avoid commands that explicitly display or transmit API keys unless you intend to share them. Finally, prefer installing packages from a verified source and inspect what the plugin does on startup (network endpoints it contacts, files it writes, and what data it sends to 'Core').
